messages:
jen: heads up — several customers reporting spikes of 504s and p95 timeouts this morning. most errors point at the hosted gateway. sample request id: req-4b2f9a. see logs attached below.

mike: thanks. are these correlated to any deploys or config changes?

jen: no deploys AFAIK. spike started ~08:12PT. error pattern: 504 from gateway, then internal service logs show "batcher_enqueue_timeout" and "queue_depth high".

liam: sharing the rough repro we got from Customer A:
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw/large-v1","input":"short prompt","max_tokens":512}'
```
response: 504 after ~22s, gateway log: `gateway: request timed out waiting for continuous batch (batch_id=cb-91f3)`

sre-elaine: tagging metrics I pulled: queue_depth_per_shard spiked from 20->380 on shard-7 around 08:10. continuous_batch_backlog increased and we see kvcache-misses up 3x. looks like prefix cache thrash causing batching stalls.

ops-bot: alert: ingress-queue-depth>300 on shard-7 (08:11). auto-shed policy not triggered because tenant below throttle threshold.

mike: can you paste the gateway trace for req-4b2f9a?

liam: trace excerpt: `gateway->ingress-queue enqueue_time=12000ms wait_for_batch=22000ms deadline_exceeded`. Also see `cbatcher: deferred_enqueue_count=412`.

jen: customers are getting error 504s in prod and raising tickets. CS Amber is on the thread. Amber, can we get a prioritized list of affected customers?

customer-success-amber: sending list now — three high-usage tenants (AcmeInc, SnapDesk, BrightDoc). AcmeInc is on a nightly job hitting longer sequences.

sre-elaine: quick mitigation suggestions: 1) increase gateway per-shard queue_depth cap from 400->800 temporarily 2) enable early_reject for sequences >400 tokens to avoid clogging continuous batch 3) roll up kvcache warmup on shard-7 (prefill prefixes for AcmeInc patterns)

mike: +1 to early_reject. runtime config is controlled by infra feature-flag `ingress.queue_limits`. I can toggle a temporary bump. leaning to early_reject + route AcmeInc to dedicated capacity if they need longseq.

liam: repro steps I ran (local sim): spawned 120 parallel clients with longseqs (avg 800 tokens). queue_depth shot up and batcher blocked on kvcache miss thrash. increasing kvcache size helped a bit but not enough.

jen: any risk to toggling queue caps? could cause memory pressure on shard.

sre-elaine: risk yes — but short window adjustment (<30m) should be safe if we monitor GPU mem and batcher latencies. set an alarm rollback if mem>85% or p95 request time grows on short-path.

mike: starting with early_reject for >400 tokens on hosted gateway, and enabling a temporary per-tenant bypass to route AcmeInc to secondary pool (lower-util dedicated burst). will post when changed.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: flag `ingress.queue_limits.early_reject.longseq=true` toggled by mike at 08:27PT.

liam: immediate effect: p95 host gateway latency dropped from 2.8s->1.0s on short-path, queue_depth on shard-7 down to 90. still seeing deferred_enqueue_count but trending down.

customer-success-amber: AcmeInc acknowledges fewer failures but requests a mitigation plan for scheduled jobs.

jen: follow-ups: - run a kvcache warmup job for AcmeInc patterns (liam) - evaluate increasing kvcache capacity on shard-7 (infra) - longer term: implement per-tenant longseq routing to Dedicated or Private (product + infra)

sre-elaine: logging note — we should add a specific metric `cbatcher.deferred_enqueue_rate{tenant}` so we can alert per-tenant before global saturation. filing a ticket.

mike: closing loop: early_reject toggled off at 08:55 after stabilization, shard-7 queue_depth steady ~60. I'll open a PR for a safer default early_reject threshold.

jen: thanks team. I'll update customers and mark as mitigated. runbook links: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/ingress-queue-saturation and https://wiki.redwood.ai/playbooks/longseq-routing.

sre-elaine: adding postmortem note: cause = sudden longseq job from AcmeInc + kvcache miss cascade -> continuous batch backlog -> gateway timeouts. mitigation = early_reject + routing + kvcache warmup.

mike: any remaining action items?

liam: I'll schedule kv warmup for AcmeInc tonight and collect reprs.

customer-success-amber: customers updated. no further escalations for now. :thumbsup:
